text:
helen: heads up — noticing a spike in tail latency from the eu-west GPU pool around 02:10 UTC. Grafana panels show long runtime spans and a pileup at the otel-gateway. suspect header bloat + batching/backpressure. anyone oncall? :eyes:
aj: on it, checking logs and prom right now. can you paste the panel link?
helen: https://grafana.redwood/eu/d/pool-health/eu-gpu-pool?orgId=1&panelId=7
infra-bot: alert fired: OTEL_GATEWAY_5XX_RATE (instance=otel-gw-eu, value=7.2) at 2025-03-05T02:12:14Z
tomas: do we have traces showing oversized headers from runtime -> gateway? last time gzipped payloads + baggage pushed header sizes >64k and nginx started dropping.
aj: pulling collector logs. saw repeated errors: 
```
2025-03-05T02:11:58Z otel-gateway[main] WARN http: request header too large: read on connection
2025-03-05T02:12:01Z runtime-proxy ERROR upstream timeout, downstream busy
```
shay: we got a spike in baggage from the new eval harness — they pass full prompt ids + input hashes as baggage which exploded size. cost impact: tracing storage jumped ~30% last week for eu traces. we should sample more aggressively for batch/stream endpoints.
helen: agree. proposal: gate-level sampling at otel-gateway: 5% for streaming inference endpoints, 20% for standard generation, 100% for canary models. also enable max_header_bytes on nginx to 128k temporarily?
aj: nginx default is 8k for some proxies; our frontend nginx has 64k. otel-gw is behind envoy which has `header_size` limit. updating envoy is safer.
tomas: here's a suggested collector fragments to reduce footprint (canary in eu):
```
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      http: {}
processors:
  tail_sampling:
    policies:
      - name: keep_canary
        type: always_sample
        # keep specific model tags
  attributes:
    actions:
      - key: large_baggage
        action: delete
exporters:
  otlp/secure:
    endpoint: traces-storage.eu:4317
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [tail_sampling, attributes]
      exporters: [otlp/secure]
```
shay: we also should add a prometheus rule to alert on `sum(rate(otel_exporter_sent_spans_total[5m])) by (instance) > X` to catch sudden trace volume spikes before storage bills hit finance.
infra-bot: infra-runbook: when otel-gateway fires 5xx and queue_depth > 80% — fallback routing to runtime-plain (no baggage) available. See /runbooks/otel-gw-backpressure.md
aj: I'm going to push a canary change: reduce gateway sampling and drop `x-baggage-full` header at the gateway for eu cluster. will run for 15m and measure tail lat.
helen: please also add a grafana panel for `http_request_duration_seconds` broken down by `sampled=true/false` and `route`. we need before/after comparison.
shay: noted. tagging finance-infra to eyeball cost delta: @kevin-finance FYI — we may cut trace volume and reduce S3/TSDB egress.
aj: canary patch applied: `kubectl -n infra patch deploy/otel-gateway --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"canary":"v1.1-sampling-0.05"}}}}}'`
helen: nice. monitoring panels look better already — tail p50->p95 gap shrinking. will keep oncall for 45m and follow up with a short postmortem + action items (delete excessive baggage keys, sampling defaults, update onboarding docs). :thumbsup:
ops-bot: reminder scheduled: create ticket INFRA-TRACING-523 for baggage cleanup and dataset cost audit.
helen: thanks all. next steps: (1) merge sampler config to eu, (2) add prom alert for trace-rate, (3) update runtime docs to avoid passing full prompts in baggage. I'll post follow-up notes in #eng-runtime.
